context.guidance: Do not write Personal Data or Authentication Secrets to localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies or outbound headers beyond what the session strictly needs. Keep identity in an opaque session identifier held server-side, and keep only non-Personal Data preferences in the browser. Where a value must be held client-side, protect it as Rule 6(1)(a) requires.

value.fix: Stop storing the auth token in localStorage. Remove the line `localStorage.setItem('token', data.token)` and have the server issue an opaque session identifier in a cookie with the HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict (or Lax) attributes. Keep the token or identity data server-side, mapped to that session ID, and expire it on logout or inactivity. Have the client rely on the cookie, sending it automatically with same-site requests, instead of reading a token from storage or attaching it manually to headers. Keep only non-personal preferences such as theme or language in localStorage. If a client-side value is unavoidable, encrypt it and limit its lifetime and scope as Rule 6(1)(a) requires. Also remove any code that reads `localStorage.getItem('token')` and any Authorization headers built from it, and confirm the change by testing that login sets the cookie, that the token is absent from localStorage and sessionStorage, and that authenticated requests still succeed.
